transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Samir from Redwood, I'm the AE, Claire will run the demo - Claire say hi.
[00:06] Claire: hi hi, Claire Huang, SE, thanks Maya, Ethan, Priya for carving out time. We have about 35 minutes, we'll do a quick catalog walkthrough, then benchmarks and compatibility, and leave time for Qs.
[00:20] Maya: sounds good. high level, our goal is to pick a model stack for patient-facing summaries and internal notes, main constraints are latency under 300ms p50, cost target, and SOC2 compliance.
[00:32] Claire: great, that helps. Quick note — I'm going to show the Console (Model Catalog tab) and also the API quickstart. The catalog groups open models by capability, cost profile, and hardware compatibility.
[00:45] Claire: (screen share) here is the model catalog, you can filter by architecture, seq len, and verified benchmarks. For example, we have "rw-open-7b-q4" with a verified latency profile on T4 and A100; and a family of 13B+ models.
[01:05] Ethan: quick question — do those benchmark numbers come from Redwood infra or public numbers? sometimes they're optimistic.
[01:12] Claire: good point. Benchmarks are from our testbed but we tag them by hardware and config; there's also a "reproducible benchmark" spreadsheet we can share. we'll run an identical workload on your sample to validate. (link: https://redwood.ai/bench/valencia-bench.xlsx)
[01:30] Samir: also note the catalog shows compatibility matrix — quantization level (Q4, Q8), supported sequence lengths, and recommended kernels. That helps if you need 32k context, some models are flagged as "32k compatible".
[01:45] Priya: on security: we need KMS integration and audit logs for Private deployment, also data residency in us-east-1. do you support customer-managed keys?
[01:56] Claire: yes, Private supports CMK via AWS KMS and HSM options; audit logs are available in the Console and via syslog. We'll send the SOC 2 and integration docs after the call.
[02:10] Maya: latency vs cost — we want to prioritize user experience for patient summaries (low p50) but keep cost under control. what are the tradeoffs?
[02:20] Claire: typically you choose a model family and then a quantization profile and routing policy. For example, rw-open-13b with Q4 and GPU A100 gives lower latency but higher cost; smaller 7b models or aggressive quantization reduce cost but can affect quality. Redwood Optimize suggests profiles per route based on traffic.
[02:37] Ethan: can we fall back to a cheaper model under heavy load automatically?
[02:41] Samir: yes, smart routing policies let you define primary and fallback model variants. we can set thresholds for latency/cost and route to a cheaper variant. that keeps SLAs intact.
[02:52] Claire: demoing the API: here's a generation call, streaming response, and how to set model_version, quantization parameter, and hardware hints. the SDK also surfaces 'compatibility' warnings if you request an unsupported seq len, e.g., 32k on a 7b-compact model.
[03:12] [03:15] Maya: i noticed a note about KV cache optimizations, can you explain?
[03:18] Claire: sure. KV cache management reduces tokens for repeated prefixes — it's especially useful for chat scenarios to lower cost and latency. we have automatic prefix caching for repeated prompts.
[03:30] Ethan: for our batch background jobs (record-keeping summarization), throughput matters more. can you show batching controls?
[03:36] Claire: yes, in Optimize you can set batching windows, target latency, and Redwood will suggest batch sizes and quantization. there's a UI that shows projected cost savings per 1k requests.
[03:50] [04:00] Priya: about Private deployment — do we still get the Console or is the control plane separate?
[04:05] Samir: Private can be deployed with a customer-managed control plane or we can provide a managed control plane with VPC peering. access is via SAML SSO and RBAC. Priya: ok we'll want SAML + SCIM.
[04:20] Claire: returning to the catalog, here's the compatibility matrix entry — it lists supported hardware, max seq len, known performance caveats. note sometimes the transcription shows 'K V cache' or weird tokens in auto-summaries, we've seen model-specific quirks.
[04:38] Maya: can Redwood run a benchmark straight on our infra? we can give an anonymized 1-hour traffic window.
[04:45] Claire: yes, we'll do a reproducible benchmark run. action: Ethan to share sample traffic, Claire will run the plan. we'll aim to simulate 1 hour and produce p50/p95/p99 and token-cost numbers.
[04:58] Ethan: sounds good. we'll export a small set and scrub PHI.
[05:04] Samir: pricing — there are hosted per-token rates and Dedicated reserved capacity options. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at commit; we'll send an initial pricing matrix.
[05:18] Maya: timeline — we'd like to pick a pilot model in two weeks and start a small Dedicated pilot in a month if numbers look good.
[05:26] Samir: that's reasonable. we'll follow up with pricing and recommended pilot config.
[05:32] Priya: last Q — what observability do we get for model rollouts? we need to detect regressions.
[05:38] Claire: Console has evals tied to prompt sets and regression alerts. you can associate a rollout with a prompt set and Redwood will alert on quality drops and automatically rollback per policy.
[05:50] [06:10] Maya: ok let's recap next steps.
[06:12] Samir: recap — Samir to send model catalog PDF + compatibility matrix and pricing; Claire to share benchmark spreadsheet and runbook and schedule the 1-hour latency run after Ethan shares traffic; Priya to confirm compliance contacts.
[06:25] Maya: thanks, that's helpful. we'll look at the sheet and pick preferred models.
[06:30] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs. bye.
[06:34] End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few mis-attributed speaker labels and occasional replacements (e.g., 'Red Wood' vs 'Redwood', 'K V cache' tokenization).
